publishedConstraint: Buratti et al. (2002) report an 8.0 by 3.15 km nucleus. These are not three measured axes.
method: Keep every reduced observed plate and outer boundary. Triangulate internal gaps with estimated plates. Build a rear height field below the completed front: zRear = zFront - 3150 * sqrt(distanceToOuterOutline / maximumDistanceToOuterOutline). The published width supplies an explicitly assumed depth scale, not a measured hidden surface. Rear interior chords are subdivided to avoid touching the observed sheet.
limitations: The hidden geometry is illustrative, not a released closed nucleus model.
The depth envelope inherits the observed height field and its noise; no additional geology or photometry is inferred.
Gap interpolation and every rear face are forced to the shared missing-data grid in all five datasets.
Independent USGS and DLR footprints produce different estimated closures. Measured-surface comparison excludes the estimated faces.
reduction: The USGS envelope and front are reduced together to at most 2000 native triangles. Opposite zero-volume face pairs are removed. A face involving any inferred rear vertex is always grid; all photographic and scientific texels must also lie inside the original source footprint. The resulting source-post surface is independently checked within 85 m against the original DEM. DLR retains its source front unchanged and uses its unreduced completion.
